comment: 🔴 37L.6 — the high-water mark for English left in the markup, by surface. A number may only go DOWN. `verify:sprint37l` fails when one rises, which is the half that stops C182 happening for a fourth time: sprints 19, 21 and 31 each shipped real Arabic work and none of them counted what was left, so fourteen sprints wrote English past a rule. Lowering these is the work. Raising one is a decision somebody makes on purpose, in a diff, with a reason in PLAN.md.
loweredInSprint51: 🔴 admin 301 to 297 and shared 79 to 71 is a MEASUREMENT CORRECTION, not translation work, and the difference matters. `literalsIn` matched the `>` of an arrow function followed by a type argument, so `(fn: () => Promise<State>)` counted as a visible literal named `Promise`. Twelve phantoms across seven files. Sprint 51's first instinct was to rewrite real code to please the regex, which is how a bad ratchet makes a codebase worse. `verify:sprint51` now asserts both halves: the arrow forms do not count, and five shapes of genuine literal still do, so the scanner is corrected rather than blinded.
note: The count is a FLOOR, not a total: it sees JSX text nodes and six attributes (aria-label, placeholder, title, alt, label, hint), so a string inside a ternary or passed as any other prop is still invisible to it. It is the right ratchet because it cannot be satisfied by remembering and it moves the moment somebody types a sentence into a page.

overridability.comment: 🔴 45.7 — the OTHER number, and the one C217 was actually about. A literal count says how much English is left; it says nothing about whether the English that IS translated can be changed by an administrator. Until 45.3 the answer for 72 client components was no: `I18nProvider` read the bundled dictionary and never consulted `ui_strings`, so an admin published an edit, saw the server-rendered half of a page change, and got no error on the other half. This counts components that read the dictionary as a VALUE instead of through a resolver. Zero is the only acceptable number: `useT` and `getI18n` both consult overrides, a direct `DICTIONARIES` read does not, and there is no case where bypassing is right.

loweredInSprint53: 🔴 patient 22→18, admin 297→294, shared 71→60 is a SECOND MEASUREMENT CORRECTION, of the same family as sprint 51's and found the same way: sprint 53 added a sponsor portal, the number went up, and reading WHY showed phantoms rather than English. `literalsIn` was matching the `>` of a relational operator inside a JSX expression container, so `{benefits.length > 1 ? (` captured the code between it and the next `<`, and a four-letter identifier in that code passed the letter test. Two real examples, both of which were IN the previous floor: "1 ? ( benefit.isPrimary ? (" and ") : canRequest && !open ? (". Rejected now by the punctuation only code has — `? (`, `) :`, `&&`, `||` — rather than by rejecting every parenthesis, which would also have dropped genuine prose like "VAT (14%)". VERIFIED THE SAME WAY THE FOUNDER VERIFIED SPRINT 51's: the corrected scanner was run against main at b66997b, which gave patient 18, auth 4, portal 1, admin 294, shared 60 — identical on every surface. So the drop is measurement and the sprint's own new surfaces add nothing to any floor. 🔴 And admin held at 294 rather than rising by twelve: the new operator screens for 53.6 are MessageKeys under `asponsor.`, because the rule from sprint 45 on is that a new string is a key, whatever the surrounding debt. One keyed label now sits in an admin nav of fifteen literals, which is that debt becoming visible rather than a new one.
raisedInSprint52: 🔴 admin 294→420 and shared 60→80 is a RISE, and a rise is the thing this file exists to make somebody argue for, so here is the argument. 52.3's findings walk photographed the ARABIC PATIENT SIGN-IN PAGE: heading, body and every hint in Arabic, and then "Phone number or email", "Password", "Sign in" and "Send me a code" in English — the first screen an Arabic-speaking patient ever sees, with t() called three lines away in the same file. 🔴 THE RATCHET COULD NOT SEE ANY OF IT. `literalsIn` counted JSX text plus aria-label, placeholder, title and alt. It did not count `label` or `hint`, which is how <Field> and <Submit> put text on screen in this repository, and there were 176 of those. That is the §6 family landing on the instrument built to prevent §6: a check that passed by measuring the wrong thing, where the thing it could not measure was most of the text. The blind spot was even STATED in the note above — 'a string passed as an ordinary prop is invisible to it' — next to the claim that the ratchet 'cannot be satisfied by remembering'. It could: it could be satisfied by using a label prop. A documented limitation whose cost is never counted is a limitation nobody acts on. So `label` and `hint` are counted now, by NAME rather than by 'any string prop', because counting every prop would sweep up ids, routes and variants and give a number that moves when somebody renames a variable — the exact failure sprints 51 and 53 each had to correct. The two new floors are pre-existing debt becoming visible, not debt added by this sprint. 🔴 AND THE PATIENT SURFACE WENT TO ZERO IN THE SAME DIFF. Under the corrected scanner it was 47. Ten files were keyed — auth-form, code-signin-form, prove-handle, reset-form, identity-editor, change-number, patient-editor, record-access, access-banner and the billing page — with 46 new MessageKeys in both languages. A raised floor beside an untouched surface would have been a re-measurement dressed as work; the surface the finding was about is finished.
c349: 🔴 admin 459→466 is a RISE of seven, and the seven are column headings on `/admin/vault`: Month, Subscriptions, Session fees, Income, Model spend, Left over, and the card's own title. C349 replaced two bars whose figures were reachable only by hovering a `title=` attribute with the same bars over a table that prints them. The rule 37L.3 set still holds and is why this is allowed rather than fixed: the admin console is staffed by us, in English, by decision, and it is the one surface this ratchet tracks without asking for Arabic. Lowering it is 37L.3's work and remains undone. 🔴 What would NOT have been allowed is the same seven strings on a patient or shared surface, and the reason this entry exists at all is that a rise has to be typed by a person with a sentence attached — the seven could otherwise have ridden in under a money fix nobody connected to translation.
sprint65: 🔴 admin 420→459 is a RISE and shared 80→72 is WORK, and the finding is neither number: THIS GATE HAD NOT BEEN RUN SINCE SPRINT 52. Measured on the commit before sprint 65 started, admin was already 459, shared 113, portal 2 and patient 4 — every one of them above the recorded floor, accrued across sprints 53 to 68 by fifteen sprints that each ran their own verifier and no shared pass. That is C182 happening a second time to the instrument built to stop C182, and H20's lesson exactly: a gate nobody runs is a gate nobody reads. The corrective is `npm run gates` (65.24), which runs the prose sweep, verify:claims, verify:principals and this ratchet in ONE pass, so a surface cannot drift unseen again. 🔴 THE NUMBERS, SEPARATED BY WHAT THEY ARE. patient 4→0: `linked-platforms` and `benefit-form` were keyed, and `linked-platforms` was a whole English component on a patient screen. shared 113→72: the patient-facing half of that surface was keyed — the pay flow, the 404, the expired-feedback page, the dead-join page, the booking sheet, the public profile, the radar filters and the rating form, 41 literals in the languages a patient actually reads. A MEASUREMENT CORRECTION is inside that: `literalsIn` counted the object-literal entries of an icon map (`, depression:` between a `/>` and a `<`) as visible English, fourteen phantoms in one file, which is the third of this family after sprints 51 and 53 and is rejected now by shape with a control in `verify:sprint37l`. admin 420→459 is the rise, and it is the admin console, which 37L.3 deferred by name and which is staffed in English by decision. Raising it rather than fixing it is a deliberate choice recorded here; lowering it is 37L.3's work and remains undone.
sprint71: 🔴 admin 466→524 is a RISE of 58, and here is the argument, which this file exists to make somebody type. Sprint 71 added /admin/financial-model: a thirty-six month forecast with twenty labelled inputs, a nine-column table, a payroll editor and two write controls. Fifty-eight of its strings are what `literalsIn` counts — `label` props and column headings — and a form with twenty inputs needs twenty labels, so the number is close to irreducible for the screen that was asked for. 🔴 THE TENSION IS REAL AND WORTH NAMING: sprint 53's entry above says 'a new string is a key, whatever the surrounding debt', and this does not follow that rule. It follows the one C349 and sprint 65 actually applied, which is 37L.3's: the admin console is staffed by us, in English, by decision. What tips it here is who reads this particular screen. `/admin/financial-model` is `requireRole("super_admin")` and shows salaries, runway and the month the cash runs out; it is a board pack, not an operating console, and there is no Arabic-reading audience for it to acquire. Keying fifty-eight strings for two readers who both work in English is work with no reader, and 37L.3's real debt — the operator screens the 24/7 team uses — is untouched by it either way. 🔴 AND THE SPRINT PAID FOR THE OTHER RATCHET IN FULL: admin prose went 2561→2508, DOWN by 53 while adding a whole screen, by cutting fourteen genuine walls of text across settings, the ledger adjuster, the partner manager, taxonomy, the therapist panel, radar, announcements, total view, usage, the vault and the investigate page. The two numbers moving in opposite directions is the honest result: more labelled controls, less prose to read.
sprint72: 🔴 admin 524→544 is a RISE of 20, and it is the same argument sprint 71 made one screen earlier, so here it is again rather than by reference. Sprint 72 added the OPERATING PLAN to /admin/financial-model: the Egypt beta, its cohort tables, and sliders for the five market guesses the beta exists to replace. Twenty of its strings are what `literalsIn` counts, and they are slider labels and column headings: a control without a label is not a control. The surface is `requireRole("super_admin")` and shows salaries, churn and runway; there is no Arabic-reading audience for a board pack, and 37L.3's real debt is the operator screens the 24/7 team works, which this does not touch. 🔴 AND THE PROSE RATCHET WAS PAID IN FULL AGAIN, twice over: the new screen cost 93 prose words, it was cut to 48, and six more genuine walls of text were shortened across the ledger adjuster, the partner manager, the therapist panel, taxonomy, the errors page and the settings editor. Admin went 2508→2479, DOWN again while gaining a second screen. Two sprints running, the same trade: more labelled controls, less prose to read.
sprint73: 🔴 admin 544→556 is a RISE of 12, and it is the operator's transfer queue: the payer's name, the amount, the reference, the receipt link, Confirm, Reject, and the box the rejection reason is typed into. Same argument as sprints 71 and 72, which is 37L.3's: the admin console is staffed by us, in English, by decision. 🔴 WHAT IS DIFFERENT THIS TIME, AND WORTH RECORDING: the sprint's OTHER new screen went the other way. `components/billing/pay-by-transfer.tsx` is where an Egyptian patient hands over money, it was written in a hundred words of English first, and this gate caught it against a patient floor of ZERO. It was keyed in both languages rather than argued for, so patient stays 0 and shared stays 72. A payment screen somebody cannot read is a payment that does not happen, and in this market that is most of them. The rule the two halves follow is the same one: English is a decision for the console the founders staff, and never for a screen a customer pays on.
sprint73b: 🔴 admin 556→567 and shared 72→75, and the two rises are different in kind. The admin eleven are the transfer-fields editor on `/admin/settings`: field labels, the audience chips, Up, Down, Remove, Add a field. Same 37L.3 argument as every admin rise since sprint 71 — the console is staffed by us, in English, by decision. 🔴 THE SHARED THREE ARE THE ONE WORTH ARGUING ABOUT, and they are on the SPONSOR's coverage control: 'Edit what you cover', 'Move it, then save', and the line that says how many sessions a balance covers. A sponsor is an Egyptian company's finance team, and unlike a patient they operate in English in this market — Egyptian corporate finance runs on English-language systems and contracts. That is a judgement rather than a rule, and it is written here so the next person can disagree with it: if a sponsor ever reports that their team reads Arabic, these three are the first keys to add and the floor comes back down. The line that CANNOT be in English is the patient's, and sprint 73 keyed that one rather than raising anything.
sprint73c: 🔴 shared 75→83, and the eight are the Egyptian company's payment form: Bank Transfer, how much you sent, the transfer reference, the waiting message. Sprint 73 keyed the patient's payment screen in both languages and raised nothing; this raises rather than keys, for a different reader. 🔴 If a sponsor ever tells us their team reads Arabic, these eight are the first keys to add and the floor comes straight back down. The rule that does not bend is the patient's: zero, and it is still zero.
